'''''Orobanche ramosa''''' is a species of [[broomrape]] known by the common names '''hemp broomrape'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref><ref>{{PLANTS|id=ORRA|taxon=Orobanche ramosa|access-date=30 January 2016}}</ref> and '''branched broomrape'''. It is native to Eurasia and North Africa, but it is known in many other places as an [[introduced species]] and sometimes a [[noxious weed]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Joel | first1 = D. M. | year = 2009 | title = The new nomenclature of Orobanche and Phelipanche | journal = Weed Research | volume = 49 | pages = 6–7 | doi = 10.1111/j.1365-3180.2009.00748.x }}</ref>

It is a pest in agricultural fields, infesting crops including [[Nicotiana tabacum|tobacco]],{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} [[potato]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Haidar | first1 = M. A. | display-authors = etal   | year = 2005 | title = Selective control of ''Orobanche ramosa'' in potato with rimsulfuron and sub-lethal doses of glyphosate | journal = Crop Protection | volume = 24 | issue = 8| pages = 743–47 | doi=10.1016/j.cropro.2005.01.005}}</ref> and [[tomato]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Mauromicale | first1 = G. | display-authors = etal   | year = 2008 | title = Effect of branched broomrape (''Orobanche ramosa'') infection on the growth and photosynthesis of tomato | journal = Weed Science | volume = 56 | issue = 4| pages = 574–81 | doi=10.1614/ws-07-147.1| s2cid = 85691913 }}</ref>

The plant produces many slender, erect stems from a thick root. The yellowish stems grow 10 to 60 centimeters tall and are coated in glandular hairs. The broomrape is [[parasitic plant|parasitic]] on other plants, draining nutrients from their roots, and it lacks [[leaf|leaves]] and [[chlorophyll]]. The [[inflorescence]] bears several flowers, each in a yellowish [[Calyx (botany)|calyx]] of [[sepal]]s and with a tubular white and blue to purple [[Corolla (flower)|corolla]].
